## 6. svc-gateway boundaries to prove

### 6.1 Public route boundary

`svc-gateway` may expose public product routes.

Allowed public boundary behaviors:

```text
route request
normalize public path
proxy selected request to internal service
forward safe headers
strip hop-by-hop headers
enforce body/range/query limits
return upstream status/body
return gateway-safe errors
fail closed when dependencies are unavailable
emit bounded metrics
attach correlation/request IDs
```

Forbidden public boundary behaviors:

```text
mint ROC
issue ROC
transfer ROC
burn ROC
hold ROC
capture ROC
release ROC
mutate ron-ledger
invent balance
invent receipt
invent payment finality
invent storage truth
invent index truth
invent QuickChain root
invent checkpoint
invent validator approval
invent bridge settlement
consume client-supplied QuickChain DTOs as authority
unlock paid content from cache alone
```

### 6.2 No direct wallet/ledger mutation

Gateway must not depend on mutation crates directly unless the existing design has explicit client adapters that call backend services over HTTP.

Target invariant:

```text
svc-gateway never mutates ron-ledger directly.
svc-gateway never exposes wallet mutation endpoints as its own authority.
svc-gateway never fabricates wallet receipts.
svc-gateway never fabricates balances.
svc-wallet remains mutation front-door.
ron-ledger remains durable truth.
```

Potential source guards:

```text
Cargo.toml production dependencies do not include ron-ledger as mutation authority.
No route exposes /v1/issue, /v1/transfer, /v1/burn, /v1/hold, /v1/capture, /v1/release as gateway-owned mutation.
If wallet paths exist, they must be proxy/client paths to svc-wallet and clearly not gateway-owned economic truth.
No source file creates balance fields from request headers.
No source file creates receipt_hash as proof/finality unless it is upstream-derived.
```

### 6.3 Paid-access fail-closed behavior

Gateway must reject or ignore fake paid claims.

Test concepts:

```text
Fake x-ron-paid header does not unlock.
Fake x-ron-receipt header does not unlock.
Fake query param paid=true does not unlock.
Fake request body receipt_final=true does not unlock.
Fake cache hit flag does not unlock.
Fake balance field does not unlock.
Fake QuickChain root/finality headers do not unlock.
```

Allowed unlock source:

```text
backend-derived wallet/storage/omnigate/access response
```

The exact code path depends on current gateway implementation.

### 6.4 Receipt display boundary

If gateway forwards receipts, it must treat them as upstream-derived display data, not gateway-created truth.

Test concepts:

```text
Gateway response must not invent receipt_hash.
Gateway response must not invent wallet_txid.
Gateway response must not invent state_root.
Gateway response must not invent receipt_root.
Gateway response must not invent finality.
Gateway response must not convert storage admission into payment finality.
Gateway response must not convert accounting event into balance truth.
```

Allowed:

```text
Forward upstream receipt fields if backend service returned them.
Return request ID/correlation ID.
Return route/service status.
Return access denied / payment required / dependency unavailable.
```

### 6.5 Cache boundary

If gateway caches responses or allows browser/client caching, it must not treat cache as paid authority.

Test concepts:

```text
Cache-Control or ETag does not imply paid unlock.
Client-supplied If-None-Match does not imply paid unlock.
Gateway cache metadata does not become receipt truth.
Offline cache does not unlock paid content.
Object b3 cache verifies bytes but does not prove access.
```

### 6.6 Storage proxy boundary

If gateway exposes `/o/:cid` or similar object routes:

```text
Gateway can proxy to svc-storage.
Gateway does not store bytes.
Gateway does not verify ownership.
Gateway does not mint CIDs.
Gateway does not claim paid access for raw object fetch unless upstream/service policy says so.
Gateway must preserve b3 canonicality if it validates object path itself.
```

Possible tests:

```text
Malformed b3 object route rejects or is not treated as authority.
Valid b3 path proxies or maps to storage route.
Raw object route response does not claim balance/receipt/root/finality.
Gateway source does not store object bytes as economic authority.
```

### 6.7 Omnigate boundary

If gateway calls omnigate for hydration:

```text
Gateway can call omnigate.
Gateway does not hydrate product truth itself unless explicitly designed.
Gateway does not convert omnigate metadata into payment finality.
Gateway does not mutate ledger based on omnigate response.
```

Possible tests:

```text
Omnigate route/source does not contain wallet mutation paths.
Hydration response shape does not claim gateway-owned finality.
Fake client-provided omnigate proof does not unlock.
```

### 6.8 Metrics/logging boundary

Gateway metrics/logs must be bounded and non-authoritative.

Metrics can include:

```text
route
method
status class
upstream service label
dependency status
request duration
body size bucket
cache hit/miss as bounded label if applicable
```

Metrics must not include:

```text
wallet account IDs
payer IDs
escrow IDs
receipt hashes
wallet txids
CIDs as labels
private capability tokens
state roots
receipt roots
checkpoint hashes
validator IDs
bridge proof IDs
```

Gateway logs must not include secrets or uncapped spend authority.

## 11. Architecture doctrine to keep in front of the next patch

Core internal ROC loop:

```text
ron-proto econ DTOs
→ ron-ledger truth
→ svc-wallet issue/transfer/burn/hold/capture/release/receipt
→ svc-storage/svc-gateway/omnigate paid enforcement
→ ron-accounting snapshots
→ svc-rewarder payout planning
→ wallet/ledger receipts
```

Gateway position in that loop:

```text
svc-gateway receives public/client traffic.
svc-gateway enforces route boundary.
svc-gateway calls or proxies internal services.
svc-gateway never owns economic truth.
svc-gateway never becomes chain authority.
```

CrabLink/Tauri relationship:

```text
CrabLink React owns display and user intent only.
Tauri mediates native privilege.
Gateway mode is primary.
Localhost is dev-only.
Mobile is gateway-first.
Offline cache cannot unlock paid content alone.
```

QuickChain relationship:

```text
QuickChain is future settlement infrastructure.
QuickChain is not current runtime.
QuickChain Phase 0 is not blockchain implementation.
No roots/checkpoints/validators/bridges/external settlement yet.
No gateway ledger mutation.
No omnigate ledger mutation.
No fake receipts.
No fake balances.
No fake proofs.
```

## 15. Specific source-guard strategy for svc-gateway

Because gateway crates can contain words like wallet/receipt/paid legitimately, avoid naive global bans.

Use context-aware guards.

### 15.1 Safe references

These can be safe depending on context:

```text
wallet_base_url
wallet upstream client
forwarding upstream receipt
display receipt
payment_required
paid access denied
proxy to svc-wallet
proxy to omnigate
proxy to svc-storage
```

### 15.2 Dangerous references

These should be forbidden or tightly constrained:

```text
direct ron_ledger dependency
ledger mutation function call
balance created from request
receipt hash hardcoded/generated by gateway
finality true created by gateway
state_root generated by gateway
receipt_root generated by gateway
checkpoint generated by gateway
validator approved generated by gateway
bridge settled generated by gateway
paid=true accepted from client request as authority
cache hit used as unlock authority
```

Core doctrine:

```text
determinism before distribution
DTOs before roots
roots before validators
proofs before pruning
internal ROC before external anchors
```

Canonicalization doctrine:

```text
canonical JSON v1
preimage = domain_separator_bytes || 0x00 || canonical_payload_bytes
hash = blake3-256 as b3:<64 lowercase hex>
money = integer minor-unit strings only
no floats
no placeholder hashes
vectors move sketch -> locked_bytes -> locked_hash
```

State/event doctrine:

```text
operation_id = backend-assigned durable ledger operation identity
idempotency_key = retry/dedupe key only, not authority
account_sequence = ledger-assigned
hold_id = one hold lifecycle
expiry = epoch-based
raw engagement must never directly mint or allocate protocol ROC
accounting is not balance truth
rewarder plans payouts but never mutates ledger
no pruning before DA/challenge/archive fallback
ROX/Solana/external L2/external bridge/external settlement remain future/deferred
anchors must not mutate ROC balances or replace wallet/ledger truth
```

## Next crate: `omnigate`

### Why `omnigate` is next

`omnigate` sits immediately behind `svc-gateway`.

It is the product/hydration coordination layer and touches the riskiest economic-adjacent flows:

```text
paid storage
paid content view
site visit quote/pay
stream-lite viewer access
chat send/quote
asset prepare/publish
wallet display/proxy paths
storage/index hydration
crab/b3 resolution
creator pages
media and manifest hydration
```

Because `omnigate` coordinates so much, it is the next likely place where accidental fake authority could creep in.

The next session should make `omnigate` prove:

```text
omnigate is hydration/product coordination boundary
omnigate is not ledger truth
omnigate is not wallet truth
omnigate is not receipt truth
omnigate is not balance truth
omnigate is not QuickChain root authority
omnigate is not checkpoint authority
omnigate is not finality authority
omnigate is not validator authority
omnigate is not bridge authority
omnigate does not unlock paid content from cache/caller claims alone
```

### Critical distinction for `omnigate`

Unlike `svc-gateway`, `omnigate` may legitimately coordinate wallet-facing paid flows.

So do not blindly ban every `svc-wallet` reference if the current architecture uses a wallet client.

The correct rule is:

```text
omnigate may call the configured wallet service/front-door for explicit paid flows.
omnigate must not mutate ron-ledger directly.
omnigate must not fabricate wallet receipts.
omnigate must not calculate balances as truth.
omnigate must not claim finality.
omnigate must not convert caller/cache claims into paid unlock authority.
```

Correct flow:

```text
client
→ svc-gateway
→ omnigate
→ svc-wallet
→ ron-ledger
→ backend receipt
→ omnigate/gateway relay display context
→ CrabLink render/unlock based on backend truth
```

Forbidden flow:

```text
client/cache/header/query
→ omnigate decides paid=true
→ unlock without backend wallet/receipt truth
```

Forbidden flow:

```text
omnigate
→ direct ron-ledger mutation
```

Forbidden flow:

```text
omnigate
→ fake receipt_id / fake receipt_hash / fake finalized=true
```

## Current QuickChain doctrine to preserve

QuickChain is future settlement infrastructure. It is not current runtime infrastructure.

Current active doctrine:

* Determinism before distribution.
* DTOs before roots.
* Roots before validators.
* Proofs before pruning.
* Internal ROC before external anchors.
* Internal ROC economy is the active proving ground.
* External settlement is deferred.
* ROX is deferred.
* Solana is deferred.
* Public bridges are deferred.
* Staking is deferred.
* Liquidity/exchange-facing logic is deferred.
* Validators are deferred.
* Anchors are deferred.
* QuickChain roots/checkpoints are deferred until canonical bytes and golden vectors exist.
* No fake hashes.
* No placeholder hashes.
* No fake roots.
* No root-producing code without canonical bytes and locked golden vectors.
* No DB-order roots.
* No wall-clock roots.
* No unknown consensus fields.
* No public chain authority inside product/service crates.

Allowed now:

* Docs hardening.
* Threat-model hardening.
* Boundary tests.
* Preflight scripts.
* DTO shape discussion.
* Strict `ron-proto::quickchain` DTO scaffolding when explicitly requested and safe.
* Validation helpers.
* Schema constants.
* Unknown-field rejection.
* Integer minor-unit strings.
* Lowercase canonical b3 validation.
* Event-class enum work.
* Operation/idempotency tests.

Forbidden until later gates are green:

* Roots.
* Checkpoints.
* Validators.
* Pruning.
* Settlement.
* Anchors.

* Liquidity.

## Current value-plane model

The RustyOnions internal ROC value plane remains:

```text id="i7xzmf"
ron-proto econ DTOs
    -> ron-ledger truth
    -> svc-wallet mutation front-door
    -> svc-storage / svc-gateway / omnigate paid enforcement
    -> ron-accounting snapshots
    -> svc-rewarder payout planning
    -> wallet/ledger receipts
```

Important crate roles:

* `ron-proto` defines DTOs.
* `ron-ledger` owns economic truth.
* `svc-wallet` is the mutation front-door.
* `svc-storage` owns paid byte storage enforcement.
* `svc-gateway` is the public boundary.
* `omnigate` coordinates hydration/product flows.
* `svc-index` owns lookup/pointers/index surfaces.
* `ron-accounting` reports snapshots, not live balances.
* `svc-rewarder` plans payouts, never mutates ledger.
* `ron-policy` defines declarative policy, not payment truth.

`svc-index` must fit into this model cleanly. It must not blur pointer truth with economic truth.

## Next crate: `svc-index`

## `svc-index` mental model

`svc-index` is not economic authority. It is lookup/pointer infrastructure.

The safest mental model:

```text id="941h3b"
svc-index tells clients and services where things point.
svc-index does not tell them who has paid.
svc-index does not prove receipt truth.
svc-index does not prove balance truth.
svc-index does not unlock paid content.
svc-index does not mutate ROC.
svc-index does not become QuickChain root/checkpoint/validator infrastructure.
```

`svc-index` may be authoritative for certain lookup/pointer records within its own domain, but that is **index/pointer truth**, not economic truth.

This distinction is subtle and important:

* `svc-index` can say: “this named site points to this manifest.”
* `svc-index` can say: “this asset b3 points to this manifest b3.”
* `svc-index` can say: “this profile handle points to this public profile record.”
* `svc-index` can say: “this creator page references these assets.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this user has paid.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this receipt is final.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this balance is true.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this object is unlocked.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this state root is canonical.”
* `svc-index` cannot say: “this checkpoint is finalized.”
* `svc-index` cannot replace wallet/ledger truth.

`svc-index` is high-risk because index records are easy for UI/product code to treat as authority. We need to prevent that early.

## Why `svc-index` matters for QuickChain

`svc-index` is one of the most important Phase-0 crates because lookup systems often become accidental authority systems.

In RustyOnions/CrabLink:

* Names are pointers.
* b3 hashes are content truth for bytes.
* Wallet/ledger receipts are economic truth.
* Manifests describe content and policy.
* Indexes help find things.
* Policy describes allow/deny constraints.
* None of those replace wallet/ledger truth.

`svc-index` must preserve:

```text id="hp7v40"
Names are pointers.
b3 hashes are byte/content truth.
Wallet/ledger receipts are economic truth.
Index entries are lookup truth only.
```

Potential risk if `svc-index` is not hardened:

* A named site pointer could be treated as ownership proof.
* An asset manifest pointer could be treated as paid-access proof.
* A profile pointer could be treated as wallet authority.
* A public index listing could leak or imply paid entitlements.
* A cached index entry could unlock content without wallet receipt.
* A future “proof” field could accidentally become fake root/finality.
* Index insertion order could later be mistaken for deterministic state order.
* A route could accidentally expose `/root`, `/checkpoint`, `/validator`, or `/quickchain` semantics.
* Index metadata could smuggle receipt/balance/finality fields.

The next session should harden against those risks.

## Specific warning for `svc-index`: do not overcorrect

The hardest part of `svc-index` is that it must be authoritative for lookup without becoming authoritative for economics.

Do not write tests that imply index records are meaningless. They are meaningful. They are just not payment truth.

Correct distinction:

```text id="skdy6e"
Index record exists and resolves a name/pointer: yes, that can be index truth.
Index record proves paid access: no.
Index record proves wallet balance: no.
Index record proves receipt finality: no.
Index record proves QuickChain root/checkpoint state: no.
```

Do not ban all `paid`, `policy`, `owner`, `creator`, `recipient`, or `manifest` fields blindly. Many of these may be legitimate metadata.

Instead, ban or constrain authority-shaped use:

```text id="1f7q7u"
paid_from_index
unlock_from_index
receipt_from_index
balance_from_index
finality_from_index
checkpoint_from_index
validator_from_index
root_from_index
```

Also ban fake authority tokens and routes.

## Suggested `svc-index` docs skeleton

Use this as the conceptual basis for `docs/quickchain-preflight.md`:

```markdown id="57umou"
# svc-index QuickChain Phase-0 Preflight

svc-index is a lookup and pointer service. It is not economic authority, not wallet authority, not ledger truth, not paid-access authority, not a QuickChain runtime, not a root producer, not a checkpoint producer, not a validator, not a bridge, not staking, not liquidity, and not external settlement infrastructure.

Index records are pointer/lookup truth only. They may help resolve names, handles, profiles, sites, assets, manifests, and crab navigation targets. They do not prove payment, entitlement, wallet balance, receipt finality, ownership, checkpoint finality, or QuickChain state.

Names are pointers. b3 hashes identify bytes/content. Manifests describe content and policy metadata. None of these unlock paid content without backend wallet/ledger/storage receipt truth.

Paid access must be proven through backend wallet/ledger/storage receipt paths, not through index entries, cached lookups, names, b3 hashes, manifests, profile pointers, route metadata, or transport headers.

svc-index must never fabricate receipt IDs, receipt hashes, paid flags, unlock flags, entitlement flags, finality flags, balance fields, state roots, receipt roots, checkpoints, validators, spend authority, or capture authority.

Future QuickChain phases may require deterministic pointer snapshots or proof-eligible lookup records, but Phase 0 must not produce roots. Deterministic ordering may be prepared as a hygiene rule only; it is not canonical root production.

ROX, Solana, public bridges, external settlement, staking, liquidity, and exchange-facing logic are forbidden in svc-index during this phase.
```

## Expected likely difficulties

### 1. False positives from scanner tests

As seen in omnigate, naive scanners can fail on legitimate metadata. Avoid brittle allowlists.

Use robust approach:

* Scan production source only.
* Ignore tests/docs unless intentionally testing docs.
* Tokenize route strings/header strings carefully.
* Reject authority-shaped tokens, not all metadata tokens.
* Avoid blocking legitimate index terms.

### 2. Index is legitimately authoritative for pointers

Do not weaken the index too much. The point is to distinguish pointer authority from economic authority.

Correct:

```text id="633l2x"
svc-index is authoritative for the pointer records it owns.
svc-index is not authoritative for paid access, wallet balances, receipts, finality, roots, or checkpoints.
```

### 3. Existing DTO names may contain `owner` or `policy`

This is probably fine. Ownership/policy metadata can exist. But it cannot become direct wallet authority or receipt/finality proof.

### 4. Existing tests may use placeholder b3 strings

If existing tests use fake placeholder b3 strings, do not immediately break the crate. First document the risk and decide whether to add a focused canonical b3 test only around production validation helpers. Avoid overcorrecting test fixtures unless necessary.

### 5. Route path variations

Inspect actual routes before writing no-settlement tests. The route scanner should check string literals in route files, but avoid catching comments/docs.

## 7. Why `ron-policy` is next

`ron-policy` is the declarative policy engine/config crate.

It is strategically important because future policy rules may touch:

```text
paid access
content access
quotas
abuse controls
economics config
residency
feature gates
admission
reward eligibility
site access
creator rules
```

That makes it easy for policy to accidentally become authority.

The next session must ensure:

```text
ron-policy decides/evaluates declarative rules.
ron-policy does not mutate balances.
ron-policy does not create receipts.
ron-policy does not mint ROC.
ron-policy does not allocate ROC.
ron-policy does not prove paid access by itself.
ron-policy does not prove finality.
ron-policy does not replace wallet/ledger truth.
ron-policy does not become QuickChain runtime.
```

Correct model:

```text
Policy may say:
- deny this request
- allow this request
- require wallet/ledger receipt
- require capability
- require quota
- require region/residency rule
- require paid gate
- classify an event
- choose a config branch
- explain a decision

Policy may not say, as final truth:
- this user has paid
- this balance is correct
- this receipt is final
- this content is unlocked without wallet/ledger/storage proof
- this reward is paid
- this state root is canonical
- this checkpoint is canonical
```

## 10. Proposed `ron-policy` docs doctrine

The `ron-policy` docs should clearly say:

```text
ron-policy is declarative policy infrastructure.
ron-policy evaluates rules and returns decisions, reasons, and obligations.
ron-policy is not wallet authority.
ron-policy is not ledger truth.
ron-policy is not receipt authority.
ron-policy is not balance authority.
ron-policy is not paid-access finality.
ron-policy is not QuickChain runtime.
ron-policy is not a root/checkpoint/validator/settlement crate.
```

Core distinction:

```text
Policy decision is not economic truth.
Policy allow is not paid proof.
Policy obligation is not receipt proof.
Policy explanation is not finality proof.
Policy config is not wallet authority.
Economics policy config is not ledger mutation.
Feature flag is not settlement authority.
Residency rule is not external anchor.
```

Allowed policy truth:

```text
this rule matched
this request is allowed/denied by policy
this obligation must be satisfied
this config branch applies
this feature is enabled/disabled
this reason explains the decision
this input failed validation
```

Forbidden economic truth:

```text
this user has paid
this wallet balance is correct
this receipt is final
this content is unlocked
this reward has been paid
this checkpoint is canonical
this state root is canonical
this settlement is complete
```

Allowed paid-access relationship:

```text
Policy may require a backend wallet/ledger/storage receipt path.
Policy may deny access if required proof is absent.
Policy may allow the request to proceed after external services have proven truth.
Policy must not itself manufacture the proof.
```

Forbidden shortcut paths:

```text
policy allow → unlock
policy tag says paid → unlock
policy config says paid → unlock
policy obligation satisfied locally → receipt
policy explanation → finality
feature flag → settlement
economics config → balance mutation
```

---

## 12. Things to avoid in `ron-policy`

Do not add:

```text
new root DTOs
new checkpoint DTOs
new validator DTOs
new settlement DTOs
new bridge DTOs
fake receipt structs
fake balance structs
mock ledger truth
mock wallet truth
public chain config
external anchor config as active runtime
staking config
liquidity config
ROX config
Solana config
```

Do not write tests that create fake receipts or fake balances just to prove they are fake.

Instead, prefer:

```text
unknown-field rejection
source scans
wire-shape absence tests
docs boundary tests
decision/result non-authority assertions
```

Do not make `ron-policy` depend on `ron-ledger` or `svc-wallet`.

If `ron-policy` needs to refer to economic concepts, keep them as:

```text
opaque strings
policy keys
required proof labels
declarative obligations
non-authoritative config
```

## Active Value Loop to Preserve

The internal ROC value loop remains:

```text
ron-proto econ DTOs
→ ron-ledger truth
→ svc-wallet issue/transfer/burn/hold/capture/release/receipt
→ svc-storage / svc-gateway / omnigate paid enforcement
→ ron-accounting snapshots
→ svc-rewarder payout planning
→ wallet/ledger receipts
```

Boundaries:

```text
ron-proto = DTOs
ron-ledger = economic truth
svc-wallet = mutation front-door
ron-accounting = snapshots, not balance truth
svc-rewarder = payout planning, not mutation
svc-storage = bytes by b3
svc-index = lookup/pointers
svc-gateway = public boundary
omnigate = hydration/orchestration
ron-policy = declarative policy
CrabLink/Tauri = client display/user intent, not backend truth
```

## Potential Workspace Gate Order

Recommended order:

```text
1. ron-proto
2. ron-ledger

4. ron-accounting

6. svc-storage
7. svc-gateway
8. omnigate
9. svc-index
10. ron-policy
```

Reasoning:

```text
ron-proto first because DTOs are the boundary vocabulary.
ron-ledger second because ledger is economic truth.
svc-wallet third because wallet is mutation front-door.
ron-accounting after wallet/ledger because accounting is snapshot/projection.
svc-rewarder after accounting because rewarder plans payouts.
svc-storage after rewarder because paid storage enforcement depends on wallet/economics boundaries.
svc-gateway after storage because gateway is public boundary.
omnigate after gateway because it hydrates/orchestrates.
svc-index after omnigate/gateway because it resolves lookup/pointers.
ron-policy last because it is declarative policy and should remain non-authoritative across all of the above.
```

Alternate order is acceptable if existing scripts/dependencies require it, but the script should be stable and documented.

## Current IoT Interpretation

RustyOnions is plausible for IoT gateway nodes, not tiny bare-metal microcontrollers.

Correct IoT model:

```text
tiny device / sensor / camera
→ sends bounded event/data/media chunk
→ local RustyOnions gateway or micronode verifies b3/cache/policy
→ backend wallet/ledger remains economic authority
```

Do not run full RustyOnions on:

```text
ESP32
Arduino
bare-metal microcontrollers
tiny sensors with no OS/TLS/process supervision
```

Good IoT roles:

```text
sensor client
camera client
event emitter
media source
metering source
analytics source
offline queue source
```

Good RustyOnions IoT gateway roles:

```text
b3 verification
bounded cache
local ingest
policy checks
offline queueing
forwarding to gateway/backend
read-only receipt display
metering event submission
```

Forbidden IoT behavior:

```text
local fake balances
local fake receipts
silent spend
cache-only paid unlock
QuickChain roots
validators
settlement
bridges
staking/liquidity
ROX/Solana
IoT device as default wallet authority
```

```text
--features quickchain-preflight
```

The low-disk runner fixed this. After the fix, ron-ledger ran real focused QuickChain tests, including atomic execution, balance transitions, replay, holds, projections, state snapshots, retry-after-accepted rebuilds, terminal hold evidence, and chain binding.

## 6. Low-Disk Runner Outcome

A new low-disk validation approach was introduced because full workspace builds were putting too much pressure on disk space.

The low-disk strategy:

```text
uses per-crate isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR
turns off incremental compilation
sets debuginfo to 0
cleans each crate target after its gate
avoids one massive workspace target directory
```

This makes the QuickChain gate practical on the current MacBook environment.

The important behavior:

```text
.quickchain-target-lowdisk/<crate>
```

is created per gate and removed after the gate passes.

This prevents target growth from accumulating across the entire workspace.

## 10. What This Phase Proves

This phase proves the following across the RustyOnions value plane:

```text
QuickChain is not accidentally live.
QuickChain is not currently a public chain.
QuickChain does not mutate balances.
QuickChain does not unlock paid content.
QuickChain does not replace svc-wallet.
QuickChain does not replace ron-ledger.
QuickChain does not turn gateway/omnigate/storage/index/policy/rewarder into economic authorities.
QuickChain fields cannot be smuggled into request DTOs.
Fake roots/receipts/balances/finality are rejected.
Raw engagement cannot directly mint or allocate ROC.
Rewarder plans payouts but does not mutate ledger truth.
Accounting snapshots are artifacts, not balance truth.
Storage b3 identity is not paid proof.
Index lookup is not ownership/payment proof.
Policy decision is not receipt/finality truth.
```

This is exactly what Phase-0 / QC-0A was supposed to prove.

## 18. Final Closeout Statement

This phase was important because it prevented QuickChain from becoming architecture creep.

Instead of prematurely building a blockchain runtime, this phase hardened the RustyOnions value plane around the correct authority boundaries:

```text
ron-ledger owns economic truth.
svc-wallet is the mutation front-door.
ron-accounting records snapshots but is not balance truth.
svc-rewarder plans payouts but does not mutate.
svc-storage stores bytes and enforces paid admission through backend truth.
svc-gateway is public boundary, not ledger authority.
omnigate hydrates views, not economic truth.
svc-index points to things, not ownership/payment truth.
ron-policy decides policy, not finality.
ron-proto defines strict DTOs and vectors.
QuickChain remains future settlement infrastructure.
```

This is a strong Phase-0 finish.

# 13. Canonical Hashing Rules to Preserve

The canonical hashing rules remain:

```text
canonical JSON v1
preimage = domain_separator_bytes || 0x00 || canonical_payload_bytes
hash = blake3-256(preimage)
hash format = b3:<64 lowercase hex>
money = integer minor-unit strings only
no floats
no JSON numeric money
unknown fields reject
b3 lowercase only
```

Vector lifecycle:

```text
sketch → locked_bytes → locked_hash
```

No fake hashes:

```text
No placeholder b3 values.
No invented hashes.
No all-zero hashes.
No TODO hashes.
No sample hashes pretending to be locked vectors.
```

---

# 14. State/Event Semantics to Preserve

Current semantics:

```text
operation_id = backend-assigned durable ledger-operation identity
idempotency_key = retry key, not authority
account_sequence = ledger-assigned
hold_id = one hold lifecycle
expiry = epoch-based
event_class = economic_receipt | metering | proof_eligible | ad_budgeted | analytics_only
```

Raw engagement rule:

```text
Raw engagement must never directly mint or allocate protocol ROC.
```

Accounting rule:

```text
Accounting is not balance truth.
```

Rewarder rule:

```text
Rewarder plans payouts but never mutates ledger.
```

Pruning rule:

```text
No pruning before DA/challenge/archive fallback design.
```

External anchor rule:

```text
Anchors must not mutate ROC balances or replace wallet/ledger truth.
```

# Immediate next pair: svc-wallet + ron-accounting

## Why this pair is next

This is the correct next pair after `ron-proto + ron-ledger`.

`ron-proto` now defines strict DTO/vector truth.

`ron-ledger` now proves deterministic execution/replay/projection truth.

The next question is service boundary truth:

```text
Does the wallet service mutate through the correct backend path,
and does accounting remain derived/read-only instead of becoming balance truth?
```

This pair is the most important remaining internal-economy gate.

---

## svc-wallet role

`svc-wallet` is the mutation front door.

It should be the controlled service surface for:

* issue
* transfer
* burn
* hold open
* hold capture
* hold release
* hold expiry
* quote/prepare
* explicit confirmation
* receipt creation/return
* balance refresh/readback through backend truth

`svc-wallet` must not:

* fabricate balances
* fabricate receipts
* silently spend
* perform hidden holds/captures
* accept client-assigned account sequences
* treat idempotency keys as authority
* create QuickChain roots
* create QuickChain checkpoints
* run validators
* anchor externally
* bridge externally
* expose raw spend authority
* store private keys/seeds in unsafe places
* let React/TS or client-side code become economic truth
* let display-only receipts become verification truth

Expected wallet doctrine:

```text
prepare/quote -> explicit confirmation -> backend wallet path -> backend receipt -> unlock/render -> display-only receipt cache -> balance refresh
```

The wallet path must remain explicit and backend-owned.

---

## ron-accounting role

`ron-accounting` is snapshot/reporting/aggregation.

It must be read-only with respect to economic truth.

It may:

* read accepted wallet/ledger-derived events
* derive snapshots
* derive reports
* seal accounting windows
* compute deterministic summaries
* expose audit-friendly snapshot DTOs
* support rewarder planning inputs

It must not:

* mutate wallet balances
* mutate ledger state
* issue ROC
* transfer ROC
* burn ROC
* open/capture/release holds
* fabricate receipts
* decide spend authority
* become balance truth
* act as settlement
* create QuickChain roots
* run validators
* anchor externally
* replace `ron-ledger` or `svc-wallet` as truth

Accounting doctrine:

```text
accounting snapshots are evidence/reporting, not balance truth
```

Test goal:

Test goal:

## 4. Balance truth boundary

Test goal:

Balances are backend/ledger truth, not UI/accounting estimates.

What to check:

* No hardcoded balances in production service code.
* No fallback fake balance.
* No local optimistic balance treated as truth.

# Bash-only preflight pattern to reuse

For each crate, prefer this style:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/../../.." && pwd)"
cd "${repo_root}"

fail() {
  printf '<crate> quickchain preflight failed: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  exit 1
}

[ -f crates/<crate>/Cargo.toml ] || fail "repo root detection failed"

if find crates/<crate> -type f -name '*.py' | grep -q .; then
  find crates/<crate> -type f -name '*.py' >&2
  fail "<crate> QuickChain tooling must stay bash-only"
fi

cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check

# Run focused tests or discovered tests, depending crate state.
# Prefer discovery when there are multiple quickchain_*.rs integration tests.

cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings

printf '<crate> quickchain preflight gate passed\n'
```

If the crate needs a feature gate similar to `ron-ledger`, use it consistently:

```bash
cargo test -p <crate> --features quickchain-preflight --test <test_name>
cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --features quickchain-preflight -- -D warnings
```

Do not assume feature gating until the codebundle is inspected.

# 4. Mental model for the next pair

## `svc-storage`

`svc-storage` owns storage behavior, byte retrieval, b3-backed asset integrity, and storage-side metering/export boundaries.

It may:

```text
store bytes
retrieve bytes
serve byte ranges/segments
verify canonical b3 hashes
return storage metadata
emit usage/metering events
provide storage evidence to accounting
enforce local storage constraints
participate in paid access only through backend wallet/gateway policy path
```

It must not:

```text
mint ROC
transfer ROC
burn ROC
hold/capture/release ROC
issue wallet receipts
invent balances
invent receipts
unlock paid content from cache alone
act as policy authority
act as wallet authority
act as ledger authority
act as QuickChain root authority
act as checkpoint authority
act as validator authority
act as settlement authority
act as bridge/anchor authority
```

Storage truth is about bytes and hashes.

Economic truth remains:

```text
ron-ledger
```

Wallet mutation remains:

```text
svc-wallet
```

Paid access orchestration remains:

```text
svc-gateway / omnigate / wallet path
```

Accounting remains:

```text
ron-accounting derivative metering/snapshots
```

`svc-storage` may emit events that later become accounting inputs, but those events are not balances, not receipts, not payouts, and not QuickChain roots.

## `svc-rewarder`

`svc-rewarder` owns reward planning.

It may:

```text
consume accounting planning artifacts
consume reward projection snapshots
calculate payout plans
validate payout plan DTOs
reject malformed/poisoned reward inputs
produce deterministic planning artifacts
prepare proposed payout plans for later wallet execution
```

It must not:

```text
mutate ron-ledger
call ledger commit directly
mint ROC
transfer ROC
burn ROC
hold/capture/release ROC
issue wallet receipts
treat raw engagement as protocol ROC authority
treat accounting snapshots as balance truth
treat reward snapshots as roots
settle payouts directly
anchor payouts externally
bridge payouts externally
stake
provide liquidity
produce QuickChain checkpoints
produce QuickChain roots
run validators
```

Rewarder output is planning, not mutation.

The only eventual legitimate economic mutation path is:

```text
ron-accounting snapshot/report
        ↓
svc-rewarder payout plan
        ↓
explicit approval / policy gate
        ↓
svc-wallet mutation request
        ↓
ron-ledger economic truth
        ↓
backend-derived wallet receipt
```

`svc-rewarder` must never skip directly to ledger mutation.

# 9. Pair-level boundary: `svc-storage` → `ron-accounting` → `svc-rewarder` → `svc-wallet`

This pair is important because it forms the future earning loop.

The safe version of the loop is:

```text
svc-storage serves/stores bytes and emits metering facts
        ↓
ron-accounting records/seals derivative usage snapshots
        ↓
svc-rewarder consumes eligible planning artifacts
        ↓
svc-rewarder creates deterministic payout plans
        ↓
explicit approval/policy gate
        ↓
svc-wallet executes actual wallet mutation
        ↓
ron-ledger records economic truth
        ↓
wallet receipt is returned
```

The unsafe version must be prevented:

```text
storage event
        ↓
direct reward
        ↓
direct ledger mutation
        ↓
fake payout receipt
```

Never allow that.

The next session should enforce this boundary in docs/tests/scripts.

# 10. Specific risk areas to watch

## Risk 1 — Rewarder accidentally becoming mutation authority

Bad pattern:

```text
svc-rewarder calculates reward and calls ledger directly.
```

Correct pattern:

```text
svc-rewarder calculates reward plan only.
svc-wallet performs mutation later through explicit backend wallet path.
ron-ledger remains truth.
```

## Risk 2 — Accounting snapshot treated as balance

Bad pattern:

```text
reward snapshot says account A earned 100 ROC, therefore account A has 100 ROC.
```

Correct pattern:

```text
reward snapshot is planning input.
Only ron-ledger balance is balance truth.
```

## Risk 3 — Raw engagement direct payouts

Bad pattern:

```text
views, likes, clicks, route wording, or analytics directly allocate ROC.
```

Correct pattern:

```text
only explicit eligible metering classes may feed planning artifacts.
raw engagement alone never allocates protocol ROC.
```

## Risk 4 — Storage CIDs treated as roots

Bad pattern:

```text
b3 artifact CID is called QuickChain root or settlement proof.
```

Correct pattern:

```text
b3 artifact CID verifies bytes only.
QuickChain roots come later under canonical byte/vector discipline.
```

## Risk 5 — Paid content unlocked by storage/cache alone

Bad pattern:

```text
local cache has bytes, therefore paid content unlocks.
```

Correct pattern:

```text
paid unlock requires backend wallet receipt/path.
cache is convenience only.
b3 verification protects bytes, not payment authority.
```

## Risk 6 — Script drift

Bad pattern:

```text
hidden Python helper scripts
hardcoded test matrices
manual one-off commands that are not encoded in crate-local preflight
```

Correct pattern:

# 2. Why `svc-gateway + omnigate` Is the Next Pair

`svc-gateway + omnigate` sits directly between clients and the backend value plane.

This pair is dangerous because it touches:

```text
public HTTP/API ingress
paid access decisions
content hydration
storage fetches
wallet receipts
index/name/content lookup
policy decisions
cache behavior
CrabLink/Tauri display flows
```

If hardened incorrectly, this pair could accidentally become:

```text
fake wallet
fake ledger
fake paid unlock authority
fake receipt issuer
fake finality layer
fake chain gateway
fake bridge surface
fake validator API
cache-only entitlement system
client-controlled paid unlock path
```

The next session should prevent those failure modes.

## Pair-Level Boundary

The safe conceptual flow is:

```text
CrabLink/Tauri user intent
        ↓
svc-gateway public boundary
        ↓
omnigate hydration/access composition
        ↓
svc-storage bytes by b3
svc-index lookup/pointers
ron-policy policy decisions
svc-wallet wallet/receipt path
ron-ledger durable truth
ron-accounting usage snapshots
svc-rewarder payout planning
```

The unsafe flow to prevent is:

```text
client header/cache/local state
        ↓
svc-gateway or omnigate
        ↓
fake paid unlock / fake receipt / fake balance / fake finality
```

The next pair must preserve:

```text
backend truth first
wallet/ledger truth for economics
b3 truth for bytes
policy truth for declarative access
index truth for lookup/pointers
gateway/omnigate as boundary/hydration, not authority
```

# 5. `svc-gateway` Mission

## Current Role to Preserve

`svc-gateway` is the public boundary.

It may:

```text
terminate public API ingress
route requests
proxy requests
apply public-boundary checks
enforce fail-closed access behavior
coordinate with backend services
forward backend-derived receipts/display data
return HTTP errors
apply bounded transport/header policy
expose health/readiness/version/metrics if present
```

It must not:

```text
mint ROC
issue ROC
transfer ROC
burn ROC
hold ROC
capture ROC
release ROC
mutate ron-ledger
invent wallet receipts
invent balances
invent paid access
invent finality
invent roots
invent checkpoints
act as validator
act as bridge
act as external settlement authority
unlock paid content from client/cache/header claims alone
treat b3 as payment proof
treat crab:// navigation as economic authority
treat transport headers as trust roots
```

## Gateway Boundary Sentence

Use this sentence in docs/tests:

```text
svc-gateway is the public boundary; it may route, proxy, and fail closed, but it must not become wallet, ledger, receipt, balance, root, finality, validator, bridge, cache, or external settlement authority.
```

## Gateway Core Invariants

The gateway preflight should prove:

```text
Gateway does not invent receipts.
Gateway does not invent balances.
Gateway does not invent roots.
Gateway does not claim finality.
Gateway does not expose validator approval.
Gateway does not claim bridge settlement.
Gateway does not mutate ledger directly.
Gateway does not mutate wallet directly except through explicit upstream service calls if such proxy behavior exists.
Gateway does not treat cache hits as paid unlock authority.
Gateway does not treat client headers as entitlement truth.
Gateway does not treat b3 as payment proof.
Gateway does not treat crab:// as authority.
Gateway does not unlock paid content without backend-derived wallet/ledger truth.
Gateway paid access fails closed.
Gateway public responses are display/proxy results, not economic truth.
```

# 6. `omnigate` Mission

## Current Role to Preserve

`omnigate` is the hydration/composition/access orchestration layer.

It may:

```text
hydrate content views
compose product/page/media responses
coordinate lookup, storage, policy, wallet-derived access info
prepare display data for CrabLink/Tauri or browser proof surfaces
enforce fail-closed paid hydration behavior
forward/display backend-derived receipt/access state
label display-only material honestly
```

It must not:

```text
mutate ledger
mutate wallet
mint ROC
issue ROC
transfer ROC
burn ROC
hold ROC
capture ROC
release ROC
invent wallet receipts
invent balances
invent paid access
invent finality
invent roots
invent checkpoints
act as validator
act as bridge
act as external settlement authority
unlock paid content from client/cache/local state alone
treat manifest/profile/index metadata as economic proof
treat b3 as payment proof
treat gateway headers as authority
```

## Omnigate Boundary Sentence

Use this sentence in docs/tests:

```text
omnigate hydrates and composes product/access views; it may display backend-derived truth, but it must not become wallet, ledger, receipt, balance, root, finality, validator, bridge, cache, or external settlement authority.
```

## Omnigate Core Invariants

The omnigate preflight should prove:

```text
Omnigate hydrates content/views.
Omnigate does not mutate ledger.
Omnigate does not mutate wallet.
Omnigate does not invent receipts.
Omnigate does not invent balances.
Omnigate does not invent roots.
Omnigate does not claim finality.
Omnigate does not expose validator approval.
Omnigate does not claim bridge settlement.
Omnigate enforces paid access only from backend truth.
Omnigate cannot unlock paid content from client/cache alone.
Omnigate cannot become chain authority.
Omnigate metadata is not economic proof.
Omnigate b3 references are byte/content references only.
Omnigate profile/site/product manifests are not payment authority.
```


Do not invent file paths. Use actual fresh bundle contents.

# 7. Pair-Level Test Strategy

## Start With Gateway First

Recommended order:

```text
1. svc-gateway
2. omnigate
```

Reason:

Gateway is the public boundary. Omnigate often sits behind or alongside it as hydration/access composition. Gateway hardening first gives omnigate a cleaner public-boundary doctrine to align against.

## Do Not Patch Blindly

First inspect fresh bundles:

```text
crates/svc-gateway/CODEBUNDLE.md
crates/omnigate/CODEBUNDLE.md
```

Look for:

```text
existing quickchain docs
existing quickchain tests
existing scripts
route modules
DTOs
paid/access modules
cache modules
wallet/ledger calls
receipt fields
metrics/logging
config surfaces
current package names
```

Patch based on the actual current code.

## Prefer Small Batches

Use smaller batches:

```text
Batch 1: svc-gateway docs + script + docs/tooling tests
Batch 2: svc-gateway boundary/cache/paid/no-direct-mutation tests
Batch 3: svc-gateway final gate/parking/codebundle

Batch 4: omnigate docs + script + docs/tooling tests
Batch 5: omnigate boundary/hydration/cache/paid/no-direct-mutation tests
Batch 6: omnigate final gate/parking/codebundle
```

If time is short, do not force both crates in one giant patch.

## Dynamic Discovery Standard

Both crates should use the same script pattern as the recently parked storage/rewarder crates:

```text
find crates/<crate>/tests -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'quickchain*.rs' -exec basename {} .rs \; | sort
```

Then run:

```text
cargo test -p <crate> --test "$test_name"
```

Then run:

```text
cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets
cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Do not hardcode the focused QuickChain test list inside the executable path.

## Bash-Only Patch Delivery

Use Bash here-docs.

Do not use Python patch scripts.

Do not use unified diffs.

Do not make git part of the normal loop.

Use commands like:

```bash
cat > crates/svc-gateway/docs/quickchain-preflight.md <<'EOF'
...
EOF
```

and:

```bash
cat > crates/omnigate/tests/quickchain_preflight_docs.rs <<'EOF'
...
EOF
```

---

# 8. Important Source-Guard Strategy

Do not use naive global bans for every word.

Gateway and omnigate may legitimately contain words like:

```text
wallet
receipt
paid
access
cache
proxy
policy
storage
gateway
hydrate
```

Safe references may include:

```text
wallet_base_url
upstream wallet client
backend-derived receipt
display-only receipt
payment_required
paid access denied
proxy to svc-wallet
proxy to svc-storage
proxy to omnigate
policy decision
cache-control
etag
content b3
```

Dangerous references include:

```text
local wallet balance truth
local receipt creation
local paid unlock from cache
client-supplied paid unlock
mint/issue/transfer/burn/hold/capture/release implemented in gateway/omnigate
direct ledger mutation
state_root generated here
receipt_root generated here
checkpoint generated here
validator approval generated here
bridge settlement generated here
external anchor mutation
staking/liquidity routes
ROX/Solana runtime logic
```

The right test pattern is usually:

```text
Allow explicit upstream/display/proxy seams.
Forbid local authority.
Forbid fake authority fields.
Forbid direct mutation.
Forbid finality/root/validator/bridge claims.
```

---

# 9. Specific Gateway Threat Model

## Threat: Client Header Smuggling

A malicious client sends:

```text
x-paid: true
x-wallet-balance: 999999
x-receipt-hash: b3:...
x-finalized: true
x-unlock-from-cache: true
```

Expected result:

```text
Gateway must not treat these as entitlement truth.
Gateway must ignore/reject them or forward only as non-authoritative metadata where safe.
Paid unlock must require backend truth.
```

## Threat: Cache-Only Paid Unlock

A cache entry exists for a paid object.

Expected result:

```text
Cache hit alone does not unlock.
Backend-derived access/receipt truth is still required.
```

## Threat: Gateway Becomes Wallet

A developer adds gateway-owned endpoints like:

```text
/v1/issue
/v1/transfer
/v1/hold
/v1/capture
/v1/release
```

Expected result:

```text
Preflight should fail unless these are explicitly upstream-proxy routes with clear labels and no local mutation.
Gateway must not be wallet mutation authority.
```

## Threat: Gateway Becomes Chain Gateway

A developer adds:

```text
/quickchain/root
/checkpoint
/validator
/bridge
/finality
/stake
/liquidity
```

Expected result:

```text
Preflight should fail.
These are forbidden in Phase-0 for gateway.
```

## Threat: Gateway Logs Secrets

Gateway logs:

```text
Authorization
Bearer token
wallet receipt body
private capability
raw cookie/session token
```

Expected result:

```text
Preflight or future hardening tests should catch this.
Gateway logs/metrics should be redacted and low-cardinality.
```

---

# 10. Specific Omnigate Threat Model

## Threat: Hydration Metadata Becomes Entitlement

A content manifest says:

```text
paid: true
owner: ...
b3: ...
```

Expected result:

```text
Omnigate may display metadata.
Omnigate must not unlock paid content merely because metadata exists.
```

## Threat: Client Receipt-Looking Data

A client supplies:

```text
receipt_hash
wallet_receipt
payment_receipt
finalized
unlock_from_cache
```

Expected result:

```text
Omnigate must not accept client-supplied receipt-looking data as authority.
Receipt/access truth must come from backend wallet/ledger/access path.
```

## Threat: Offline Cache Unlock

A local/offline cache has b3-verified bytes.

Expected result:

```text
B3 verification proves byte integrity only.
It does not prove paid entitlement.
Cache cannot unlock paid content alone.
```

## Threat: Omnigate Becomes Ledger

A developer adds direct ledger mutation or direct wallet issue/capture behavior inside omnigate.

Expected result:

```text
Preflight should fail.
Omnigate must call backend services where necessary and never become economic mutation authority.
```

## Threat: Omnigate Becomes QuickChain Runtime

A developer adds:

```text
root production
checkpoint production
validator signatures
bridge settlement
staking/liquidity
external anchors
```

Expected result:

```text
Preflight should fail.
QuickChain runtime behavior is future/deferred and belongs elsewhere after gates.
```

```text
index pointers are not authority
```

# Canonical QuickChain Facts to Preserve

## Hashing / Vectors

Future vectors use:

* canonical JSON v1 first
* no fake hashes
* no placeholder hashes
* preimage = `domain_separator_bytes || 0x00 || canonical_payload_bytes`
* hash = `blake3-256`
* wire form = `b3:<64 lowercase hex>`

Vector process:

1. sketch
2. locked bytes
3. locked hash

No vector should be treated as locked until canonical bytes and real hash are generated.

## Money

Money must remain:

* integer minor-unit strings only
* no floats
* no decimal arithmetic in economic DTOs
* no UI-only formatting as source of truth

## Identity / Operation Rules

Preserve these distinctions everywhere:

* `operation_id` is backend-assigned durable ledger operation identity.
* `idempotency_key` is retry/deduplication key only, not authority.
* `account_sequence` is ledger-assigned.
* `hold_id` identifies a single hold lifecycle.
* expiry is epoch-based.
* backend wallet/ledger path owns paid receipt truth.

## Event Classes

The valid conceptual event classes remain:

* `economic_receipt`
* `metering`
* `proof_eligible`
* `ad_budgeted`
* `analytics_only`

Important: raw engagement must never directly mint or allocate protocol ROC.

# `svc-index` — Target Architecture

## Intended Role

`svc-index` is a lookup and pointer service.

It may store and resolve:

* names
* pointers
* asset-to-manifest mappings
* site-name pointers
* profile pointers
* crab:// navigation targets
* b3-addressed object references
* index metadata needed for lookup

It must not become:

* ledger
* wallet
* accounting truth
* reward allocator
* policy authority
* QuickChain runtime
* root producer
* checkpoint producer
* validator
* bridge
* external settlement participant
* paid unlock authority
* balance authority
* receipt authority

## Core `svc-index` Doctrine

The central phrase for this crate should be:

`svc-index is a lookup and pointer service, not an economic authority.`

Additional scanner-friendly phrases should include:

* `svc-index is a lookup and pointer service`
* `names are pointers, not authority`
* `index pointers are not payment proof`
* `index lookup is not balance truth`
* `index lookup is not receipt truth`
* `crab names are navigation, not authority`
* `b3 hashes are content truth, not economic truth`
* `b3 proves bytes`
* `b3 does not prove payment`
* `manifest pointers do not prove payment`
* `svc-index does not unlock paid content`
* `svc-index does not mint ROC`
* `svc-index does not transfer ROC`
* `svc-index does not mutate ledger balances`
* `svc-index does not create wallet receipts`
* `svc-index does not produce roots`
* `svc-index does not produce checkpoints`
* `svc-index does not run validators`
* `svc-index does not expose bridge routes`

## Why `svc-index` Matters

`svc-index` is dangerous in a subtle way.

It is not obviously economic, but it can accidentally become authority if pointer resolution is treated as proof of rights/payment/ownership.

The tests/docs must prevent confusion between:

* pointer existence vs ownership
* name resolution vs entitlement
* manifest pointer vs payment proof
* b3 hash vs economic proof
* indexed metadata vs ledger truth
* crab:// navigation vs authorization

## `svc-index` Paid Access Boundary

`svc-index` may return where content is.

It must not decide whether the user paid.

Paid access must still be validated through backend wallet/ledger receipt paths, normally coordinated through storage/gateway/omnigate.

Index lookup cannot unlock content by itself.

Bad behavior to prevent:

* `GET /index/foo` returns `paid: true` as authority.
* pointer metadata includes fake receipt/finality.
* index route accepts `x-ron-paid: true`.
* index route accepts `x-quickchain-final: true`.
* index lookup returns a balance.
* pointer write creates an economic receipt.
* name ownership becomes wallet ownership.
* crab:// name resolution becomes paid entitlement.

# `ron-policy` — Target Architecture

## Intended Role

`ron-policy` is declarative policy.

It may:

* parse policy bundles
* validate policy schema
* evaluate allow/deny decisions
* classify request context
* classify event context later
* provide stable decision DTOs
* provide policy reasons
* enforce deterministic decision semantics
* support gateway/omnigate/service middleware decisions

It must not:

* mutate ledger
* mutate wallet
* mint ROC
* transfer ROC
* burn ROC
* capture/release holds
* create receipts
* allocate protocol rewards
* finalize settlement
* produce roots
* produce checkpoints
* run validators
* expose bridges
* decide balance truth
* decide paid entitlement by itself
* replace backend wallet/ledger receipt validation

## Core `ron-policy` Doctrine

The central phrase for this crate should be:

`ron-policy is declarative policy, not economic authority.`

Additional scanner-friendly phrases:

* `ron-policy is declarative policy`
* `policy decisions are not balance truth`
* `policy decisions are not receipt truth`
* `policy does not mutate ledger`
* `policy does not mutate wallet`
* `policy does not mint ROC`
* `policy does not transfer ROC`
* `policy does not allocate protocol rewards`
* `policy does not create wallet receipts`
* `policy does not unlock paid content without backend receipt validation`
* `policy does not produce roots`
* `policy does not produce checkpoints`
* `policy does not run validators`
* `policy does not expose bridge routes`
* `policy may classify intent`
* `policy may allow or deny request flow`
* `policy is not settlement`

## Why `ron-policy` Matters

`ron-policy` is dangerous because an allow/deny engine can easily be mistaken for authority.

A policy decision can say:

* this request is allowed to proceed
* this request is denied
* this content is permitted under policy
* this event is classified as proof eligible

But it must not say by itself:

* this user has paid
* this user has this balance
* this receipt is final
* this ROC transfer happened
* this reward payout has been allocated
* this checkpoint/root is valid
* this unlock is economically authorized without backend receipt validation

Policy can gate flow. It cannot create economic truth.

## `ron-policy` Event Classification Boundary

Future QuickChain may use event classes:

* `economic_receipt`
* `metering`
* `proof_eligible`
* `ad_budgeted`
* `analytics_only`

`ron-policy` may eventually classify which events are allowed or eligible for downstream processing.

But:

* classification is not mutation
* `proof_eligible` is not proof
* `ad_budgeted` is not payout
* `metering` is not economic receipt
* `analytics_only` must never mint/allocate ROC
* raw engagement must never directly mint/allocate protocol ROC

## `ron-policy` QuickChain Docs Target

Add or harden:

`crates/ron-policy/docs/quickchain-preflight.md`

Suggested sections:

# Testing Philosophy for Next Session

The goal is not to write massive implementation code.

The goal is to create executable safety rails.

Each crate should prove:

* This crate knows its role.
* This crate’s docs state the role.
* This crate’s source does not import forbidden authority.
* This crate’s routes/APIs do not publish forbidden authority.
* This crate does not fabricate receipts/balances.
* This crate does not treat headers/cache/pointers/policy decisions as economic truth.
* This crate has a repeatable parking script.
* Existing product/regression tests still pass.

The tests should be scanner-style where useful, but carefully scoped to avoid false positives in:

* docs
* tests
* comments that explicitly list forbidden scope
* historical notes
* generated codebundle files

Use helper functions that collect production source files only where needed.

# Specific Risks to Watch in `svc-index`

## Risk 1 — Pointer Equals Authority

Do not allow pointer existence to imply:

* ownership
* entitlement
* payment
* receipt validity
* balance truth
* finality

## Risk 2 — Name Equals Identity Authority

A name can point to something, but it cannot by itself prove:

* passport identity
* wallet ownership
* payment rights
* creator rights
* economic ownership

Passport/wallet/backend flows must own those truths.

## Risk 3 — b3 Equals Payment Proof

b3 only proves bytes/content identity.

It does not prove:

* the user paid
* the content is unlocked
* the payer has rights
* the holder has balance
* ledger mutation occurred

## Risk 4 — Index as Paid Unlock Cache

Index metadata must not unlock paid content.

Even if metadata says a content item is paid/free, actual paid unlock requires backend validation.

## Risk 5 — Route Creep

Avoid routes like:

* `/quickchain/root`
* `/quickchain/checkpoint`
* `/quickchain/validator`
* `/quickchain/bridge`
* `/settlement`
* `/state-root`
* `/receipt-root`
* `/balance`

Unless they are explicit fail-closed/404 tests or docs naming forbidden scope.

---

# Specific Risks to Watch in `ron-policy`

## Risk 1 — Policy Equals Payment Truth

A policy decision is not a payment receipt.

`Allow` means the policy layer allows flow to continue. It does not mean the user paid.

## Risk 2 — Policy Equals Balance Truth

Policy must not produce or alter balances.

## Risk 3 — Policy Equals Reward Allocation

Policy may classify events, but must not allocate protocol ROC.

## Risk 4 — Policy Equals Settlement

Policy cannot decide finality, roots, checkpoints, validators, external anchors, or settlement.

## Risk 5 — Context Smuggling

Policy context must not blindly treat client-provided fields as authority.

If policy receives transport context, it is only context unless validated by backend truth.

## Risk 6 — Overpowered Decision DTOs

Policy output should not grow fields that look like:

* `new_balance`
* `receipt`
* `receipt_root`
* `state_root`
* `capture_hold`
* `transfer`
* `mint`
* `reward_amount`
* `finality`

If future code needs event classification, keep it classification-only.

# 5. Important Bugs / Lessons From Latest Session

## Escaping Bug in Test Repair Script

A previous Perl-based repair script produced bad Rust string escaping:

```text
""\$CARGO" fmt"
```

This caused Rust parser errors.

Resolution:

```text
Replaced both tooling-boundary tests with full clean files using Rust raw-string assertions.
Avoided further Perl escaping.
```

Lesson:

```text
For Rust test files with shell-string assertions, prefer full file replacement over fragile inline Perl escape patches.
```

## Tooling Test Was Too Literal

The scripts used:

```text
CARGO="${CARGO:-cargo}"
"$CARGO" fmt
"$CARGO" test
"$CARGO" clippy
```

The test originally looked for literal:

```text
cargo fmt
```

That failed even though the script was better and more flexible.

Resolution:

```text
Tests now validate env-aware Cargo command shape.
```

Lesson:

```text
Tooling tests should validate intended behavior, not brittle exact hardcoded command spelling.
```

## Disk Pressure Remains a Real Constraint

Prior sessions hit disk exhaustion due to repeated Cargo builds.

Known issue:

```text
Cargo target directories can become enormous during repeated test/clippy/all-target cycles.
```

Known mitigation:

```text
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
RUSTFLAGS="-C debuginfo=0"
CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/.quickchain-target-lowdisk/<crate>"
rm -rf .quickchain-target-lowdisk/<crate> after success
cargo clean -p <crate> when needed
cargo clean only when necessary
```

Carry-forward decision:

```text
Do not spend the next session building a heavy all-crate umbrella runner.
Stub or document it only.
Move to the next actual product/client boundary hardening work.
```

```text
TypeScript adapters call typed APIs.
Tauri Rust mediates native privilege.
Backend services own paid truth.
Wallet/ledger receipts unlock paid content.
Display caches remain non-authoritative.
Offline cache cannot unlock paid content alone.
No client chain authority exists.
```

Build or review a QuickChain/ROC preflight boundary layer for CrabLink Tauri and client adapters.

The goal is not to implement chain features in the client.

The goal is to prove the client cannot become:

```text
wallet authority
ledger authority
receipt fabricator
balance fabricator
paid unlock authority from cache
QuickChain root/checkpoint/validator authority
bridge authority
settlement authority
external chain authority
```

# 8. CrabLink Tauri Boundary Rules to Preserve

## Tauri / React / TypeScript Split

Correct authority split:

```text
React:
  display and user intent only

TypeScript adapters:
  typed calls to allowlisted APIs only

Tauri Rust:
  native privilege boundary, bounded commands, redaction, validation

RustyOnions backend:
  truth, paid enforcement, wallet/ledger receipts
```

Incorrect:

```text
React owns receipt truth
React owns wallet balance
React stores spend authority
TS owns secrets
TS fabricates receipts
Tauri command returns raw capabilities
Tauri command unlocks paid content from offline cache alone
client acts as QuickChain authority
```

## Tauri Command Rules

Tauri commands should be:

```text
small
typed
allowlisted
redacted
bounded
source-labeled
policy-aware
feature-gated
testable
```

Forbidden command names / patterns:

```text
run
execute
eval
shell
native
raw_*
quickchain_root
checkpoint
validator
settle
bridge
staking
liquidity
mint
issue
transfer
burn
hold
capture
release
unlock_paid_from_cache
```

Important nuance:

Some product flows may call backend wallet paths indirectly through approved service APIs, but the client must not own or fabricate those mutations.

## Secrets / Authority Must Not Reach React

React/TS must not receive:

```text
private keys
seeds
raw capabilities
spend authority
uncapped wallet authority
backend service secrets
raw auth tokens in logs
receipt signing authority
ledger mutation authority
validator keys
bridge keys
```

## Paid Flow Rules

Correct paid flow:

```text
prepare / quote
explicit user confirmation
backend wallet path
backend receipt
backend storage/gateway/omnigate paid enforcement
unlock/render
display-only receipt cache
balance refresh from backend
```

Forbidden paid flow:

```text
local UI says paid=true
local cache says paid=true
manifest says paid=true
index pointer exists
policy allow decision exists
receipt-shaped JSON exists in localStorage
offline cache has bytes
therefore unlock paid content
```

## Offline Cache Rules

Allowed:

```text
cache bytes
verify b3 before trusted render
show cached free content
show previously unlocked content only when backend/display rules allow
store display-only receipt references
```

Forbidden:

```text
offline cache alone unlocks paid content
cache entry becomes receipt truth
cache entry becomes balance proof
cache entry bypasses wallet/ledger
cache entry grants future paid entitlement
```

## Media Rules

Allowed:

```text
bounded media requests
range/segment reads
rendition-specific b3 verification
honest local preview
honest export metadata
```

Forbidden:

```text
full-file large media through command results
DRM/anti-rip claims
unbounded memory transfer
fake paid access based on local file presence
fake receipt based on export state
```

## Facets / Future Extensions

Facets remain inert until sandboxed.

Allowed:

```text
display placeholder
metadata-only listing
sandbox plan docs
explicit disabled state
```

Forbidden:

```text
facet executes code
facet receives secrets
facet mutates wallet
facet unlocks paid content
facet bypasses backend
```

## 6. `ron-proto` current role

`ron-proto` is the DTO crate.

Its job is:

```text
define strict shapes
define validation helpers
define schema constants
define canonical payload families
reject drift
reject invalid wire/data forms
```

Its job is not:

```text
execute ledger mutations
produce roots
produce checkpoints
verify validators
call services
write storage
open sockets
spawn tasks
anchor externally
```

`ron-proto` is where QuickChain vocabulary must be boring, strict, and versioned.

---

## 7. `ron-proto` facts to preserve

Preserve these doctrine facts:

```text
canonical JSON v1 first
no fake hashes
no placeholder hashes
preimage = domain_separator_bytes || 0x00 || canonical_payload_bytes
hash = blake3-256
wire hash form = b3:<64 lowercase hex>
```

Vector process:

```text
1. sketch
2. locked_bytes
3. locked_hash
```

Do not mark a vector as locked until:

```text
canonical bytes are exact
domain separator is exact
preimage framing is exact
real BLAKE3 hash is generated
independent verifier reproduces it
```

Money rules:

```text
integer minor-unit strings only
no floats
no decimal arithmetic in economic DTOs
no UI-formatted money as source of truth
```

Identity rules:

```text
operation_id is backend-assigned durable ledger operation identity
idempotency_key is retry/deduplication key only
account_sequence is ledger-assigned
hold_id identifies one hold lifecycle
expiry is epoch-based
backend wallet/ledger path owns paid receipt truth
```

Event classes:

```text
economic_receipt
metering
proof_eligible
ad_budgeted
analytics_only
```

Important rule:

```text
raw engagement must never directly mint or allocate protocol ROC
```

## 10. `ron-ledger` facts to preserve

```text
operation_id uniqueness
idempotent retry behavior

checked arithmetic
atomic balance transitions
atomic hold lifecycle transitions
```

```text
settled root

validator proof
chain state
```

It is not yet a public blockchain.

```text

DTOs before roots

internal ROC before external anchors
```

## 10.4 Event-class doctrine for accounting

QuickChain event classes:

```text
economic_receipt
metering
proof_eligible
ad_budgeted
analytics_only
```

Important meaning:

```text
economic_receipt:
  can reflect actual wallet/ledger economic receipt evidence

metering:
  usage measurement, not direct payout authority

proof_eligible:
  may be eligible for future proof/challenge systems, not immediate payout authority

ad_budgeted:
  budget/accounting context, not direct ledger mutation

analytics_only:
  analytics/reporting only, never payout mutation
```

Critical rule:

```text
raw engagement must never directly mint, allocate, or mutate protocol ROC
```

`ron-accounting` must not convert views/clicks/likes/raw engagement into direct ROC mutation.

Any future rewards must go through:

```text
accounting summary
→ rewarder deterministic payout planning
→ explicit wallet/ledger mutation path
→ backend receipt
```

No direct accounting mutation.

# 16. Important semantic reminders

## 16.1 `operation_id`

```text
operation_id = backend-assigned durable ledger-operation identity
```

It is not a retry key.

It is not user authority.

It must not be client-forged as economic truth.

## 16.2 `idempotency_key`

```text
idempotency_key = retry safety key
```

It prevents duplicate processing of the same intended operation.

It is not the source of authority.

It must not replace operation identity.

## 16.3 `account_sequence`

```text
account_sequence = ledger-assigned account sequence
```

Clients must not assign it.

Wallet/accounting must not invent it.

## 16.4 `hold_id`

```text
hold_id = identity for one hold lifecycle
```

A hold lifecycle is:

```text
open -> capture
open -> release
open -> expire
```

Terminal holds must not reopen or retransition.

## 16.5 Receipts

Receipts are backend-derived evidence from the wallet/ledger path.

They must not be fake display objects.

They must not be invented by client/cache/accounting.

## 16.6 Accounting snapshots

Accounting snapshots summarize known evidence.

They are not balance truth.

They do not mutate balances.

They do not unlock paid content.

They do not issue receipts.

## 16.7 Rewarder

Rewarder plans payouts.

Rewarder does not mutate ledger.

Rewarder output must go through wallet/ledger mutation path later.

## 16.8 Gateway/omnigate

Gateway and omnigate enforce/hydrate/display.

They must not mutate ledger truth.

They must not create fake receipts.

They must not bypass wallet.

## 5. `svc-rewarder` mission

### 5.1 Correct role

`svc-rewarder` is:

```text
deterministic payout planner
```

It may:

```text
read accounting snapshot/planning artifacts
validate reward plan inputs
reject unknown/smuggled authority fields
compute deterministic payout plans
produce planning artifacts
produce candidate payout intents
prepare handoff payloads for svc-wallet
record planning metrics
```

It must not:

```text
mutate balances
mutate wallet
mutate ledger
issue ROC
mint ROC
burn ROC
transfer ROC
hold ROC
capture a hold
release a hold
create wallet receipts
claim payout execution
claim settlement
claim finality
claim checkpoint inclusion
produce QuickChain roots
sign validator evidence
anchor externally
bridge externally
stake
provide liquidity
consume raw engagement as direct protocol ROC payout authority
```

The only valid economic execution path remains:

```text
svc-rewarder deterministic plan
→ explicit approved payout intent
→ svc-wallet
→ ron-ledger
→ backend-derived receipt
```

### 5.2 Main risks to prevent

The next session should harden against these rewarder risks:

```text
Rewarder directly calls ron-ledger mutation APIs.
Rewarder directly calls wallet write APIs without explicit handoff boundary.
Rewarder treats accounting snapshots as balance truth.
Rewarder treats funding provenance as settlement finality.
Rewarder treats raw engagement as protocol ROC.
Rewarder accepts client-supplied event_class as payout authority.
Rewarder accepts client-supplied operation_id as authority.
Rewarder accepts idempotency_key as durable operation identity.
Rewarder accepts root/checkpoint/finality fields.
Rewarder emits fake receipts.
Rewarder emits fake balances.
Rewarder emits fake finality.
Rewarder has nondeterministic plan ordering.
Rewarder uses floating-point money.
Rewarder double-plans/double-pays on replay.
Rewarder has wall-clock-dependent payout math.
Rewarder exposes validator/checkpoint/anchor/bridge/staking/liquidity vocabulary as runtime authority.
```

### 5.3 Specific boundaries to lock

For `svc-rewarder`, tests/docs should lock:

```text
Planning only, no mutation.
Funding source/provenance is not settlement.
Accounting snapshot input is not balance truth.
Reward plan output is not receipt truth.
Payout intent is not payout execution.
Raw engagement is not payout authority.
Event classes are narrow and explicit.
Unknown fields reject.
Authority-smuggling fields reject.
Money is integer minor-unit string only.
No floats.
Plan ordering is deterministic.
Duplicate/replay inputs do not create extra authority.
Idempotency key is retry/dedupe only.
Operation identity is backend-assigned.
No roots/checkpoints/validators/settlement/anchors/bridges/staking/liquidity.
No Solana/ROX/external settlement path.
```

## 6. `svc-storage` mission

### 6.1 Correct role

`svc-storage` is:

```text
byte/object storage and b3 integrity infrastructure
```

It may:

```text
store bytes
serve bytes
verify b3 content integrity
emit storage/access metering events
track object/rendition metadata
support paid storage/access flows through explicit backend receipt paths
support range/segment serving for large media
enforce bounded request/body/media behavior
feed accounting with storage/access usage
```

It must not:

```text
mutate balances
mutate wallet
mutate ledger
issue ROC
mint ROC
burn ROC
transfer ROC
hold ROC
capture a hold
release a hold
invent receipts
invent balances
unlock paid content from cache alone
treat b3 as proof of payment
treat cache hit as authorization
treat manifest possession as authorization
claim settlement
claim finality
produce QuickChain roots
produce receipt roots
produce account state roots
act as validator
anchor externally
bridge externally
stake
provide liquidity
```

Correct paid storage/access model:

```text
quote/prepare
→ explicit confirmation
→ svc-wallet hold/capture/release or transfer path
→ ron-ledger durable truth
→ backend-derived receipt
→ gateway/omnigate/storage enforcement observes backend authority
→ unlock/render/serve allowed content
→ display-only receipt cache
```

Incorrect model:

```text
has bytes
→ assume paid

has b3
→ assume paid

has cached content
→ assume paid

has manifest
→ assume paid

client says receipt_hash
→ assume paid

storage emits accounting event
→ assume paid

storage sees engagement/view
→ mint/pay ROC
```

### 6.2 Main risks to prevent

The next session should harden against these storage risks:

```text
Storage directly calls wallet/ledger mutation paths.
Storage invents payment receipts.
Storage invents balances.
Storage treats b3 as payment proof.
Storage treats manifest as payment proof.
Storage treats local cache as payment proof.
Storage unlocks paid content without backend receipt/authorization.
Storage accepts fake receipt/finality/root fields.
Storage accepts client-supplied settlement status as truth.
Storage emits accounting events that imply balance mutation.
Storage uses raw engagement as protocol ROC authority.
Storage exposes checkpoint/root/validator/bridge/anchor/staking/liquidity fields.
Storage serves large media through unbounded command/result paths.
Storage claims DRM/anti-rip guarantees.
Storage treats rendition b3 values loosely instead of each rendition owning its own b3.
```

### 6.3 Specific boundaries to lock

For `svc-storage`, tests/docs should lock:

```text
b3 hashes identify bytes, not payment.
b3 hashes are content truth only.
b3 hashes are not account roots.
b3 hashes are not receipt roots.
b3 hashes are not checkpoint roots.
b3 hashes are not proof of payment.
b3 hashes are not settlement finality.
offline/cache paths must verify b3 before trusted render.
cache cannot unlock paid content alone.
paid unlock requires backend-derived receipt/authorization.
receipt cache is display-only.
storage metering is derivative accounting input only.
storage/access metering does not mutate wallet or ledger.
storage cannot produce payout authority.
storage cannot produce roots.
large media serving must be bounded/range/segment oriented.
each rendition owns its own b3.
```

## 7. Pair-level design: `svc-rewarder + svc-storage`

This pair should be treated as the bridge from internal accounting to byte/product enforcement.

The correct shape is:

```text
svc-storage:
  proves bytes and b3 integrity;
  emits storage/access usage;
  does not decide balances.

ron-accounting:
  turns storage/access usage into derivative snapshots;
  does not decide balances.

svc-rewarder:
  turns accounting snapshots into deterministic payout plans;
  does not mutate balances.

svc-wallet:
  executes approved economic intent;
  front-door for mutation.

ron-ledger:
  durable economic truth.
```

The wrong shape is:

```text
svc-storage:
  receives traffic and pays itself directly.

svc-rewarder:
  reads engagement and mutates ledger directly.

ron-accounting:
  reports a reward snapshot and treats it as a receipt.

gateway/omnigate:
  sees a receipt-looking object and unlocks without backend authority.

CrabLink:
  treats cache/display receipt as spend authority.
```

The next pair should make the wrong shape hard to implement by accident.

---
